content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (RENEWAL, § 8.2–8.3) — no redline proposed.

The renewal provisions already hit our preferred position on every parameter:

- **Renewal term:** successive twelve-month periods — no multi-year evergreen.
- **Notice window:** Customer opt-out on thirty days' written notice (preferred ≤ 30 days), and the deadline is extended to thirty days after receipt if Vendor fails to send its reminder.
- **Reminder:** Vendor must remind Customer at least sixty days before renewal.
- **Price uplift:** capped at the lesser of trailing twelve-month CPI-U and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods.

Non-renewal is Customer's right alone, which is an asymmetry in our favour and not something to flag.

One flag for the deal team outside this rule: § 2.1 commits Customer to USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis "without reduction or termination rights." That commitment could make the § 8.2 opt-out economically hollow, since declining to renew an Order Form may not relieve the minimum spend. That belongs to the minimum-commitment / termination-rights rule rather than the renewal mechanics, so I left § 8.2–8.3 untouched.
